title: Google Voice Pricing: Plans, Rates and Costs (2026)
summary: Google Voice pricing has multiple plans with different per-user rates. Find the cost of each plan and any pricing caps that may apply to your account.
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions


### Is Google Voice free for personal use?


Yes, a personal Google Voice account with a personal Google account costs nothing for a US number, calls and texts within the US and Canada, and voicemail. That makes it a fine test of whether the service suits you.


It's not a business line: it doesn't have team features, so a company that outgrows it is paying for the business plans described earlier, priced by user count.


### Can I use Google Voice for business without Google Workspace?


No. The business version of Google Voice is sold as an add-on to Google Workspace, so each person on a Voice plan needs a Workspace account too. Add the Workspace seat cost to the Voice cost when you price your team.


Comparing only the Voice price understates the bill, and a team that doesn't yet use Workspace is buying two products at once.


### Does Google Voice charge for texts?


On the personal service, texts between US numbers aren't billed per message, and the business plans don't meter them as a separate line item. The catch is scope. Messaging works within the US, and international texting isn't what these plans are built for.


If your team texts customers abroad, check that route before committing, because a plan that handles your domestic volume may not cover your actual traffic.


### Can I keep my existing number on Google Voice?


Usually, yes. Google Voice supports porting a number in, and on the business side it's the normal way to avoid reprinting cards and notifying customers.


Eligibility depends on the carrier currently holding the number and on your account type, so confirm the number is portable before you cancel anything. Cancelling first can strand a number you can't recover. Port it, confirm it works, then close the old account.


### Does paying yearly change the Google Voice price?


It can. Google Workspace plans commonly offer a lower effective monthly rate for an annual commitment than for flexible month-to-month billing, and Voice add-ons follow similar terms.


The trade is flexibility: a yearly commitment locks in a seat count, so a team that adds or drops people pays for seats it may not use. Price your own headcount both ways, then pick yearly only if that headcount is stable.
